acceptance: A documented Docker command builds, tests, captures and compares all four architectures and publishes a combined JSON and HTML report.

completion_policy.interpretation: The requirement statuses certify the verification pipeline engineering. They do not certify that every port conforms; port_conformance remains a separate result and cannot pass while contract violations remain.

purpose: Verify that Intel Intrinsics have been ported correctly to OpenPOWER, ARM64 NEON and RISC-V64 RVV implementations, using the Intel implementation and the authenticated case contract as the reference.

port_conformance.reference: Intel Intrinsics Guide semantics, captured Intel C implementation output and the selected case comparison contract
port_conformance.rule: A target output that violates the case comparison contract is a port-conformance failure requiring investigation or correction. CPU-specific behavior can explain a mismatch but does not turn a bit-exact mismatch into a pass.

known_portable_model_findings.scope: Independent portable Python model verification; separate from target C port conformance.

verification_scope: Verification-pipeline engineering and its retained evidence. Target-port conformance is a separate unresolved verdict.

initial_full_verify.note: The running launcher file was edited during the first full verification, causing a trailing shell parse error. Its completed build, CTest and native captures were retained. Latest-source quality, canonical comparisons, strict trace reauthentication and reports were run separately after fixes. This record does not claim that the initial raw verify invocation exited successfully.

final_evidence_method: Retained actual four-target Docker build/CTest/capture results.
Ran the latest-source quality gates separately.
Ran all four architecture-specific encoded ABI suites.
Recomputed canonical comparisons and regenerated reports from corrected sources.
Reauthenticated manifests, traces, measured probes, binary/object bytes and comparison counts.
verification_record.local_evidence_policy: Evidence paths refer to ignored local run artifacts, not files embedded in the source checkout. Re-running the documented Docker workflow produces a new evidence set.
